why: Every alternative lacks vocabulary for Claude Code's hook JSON schema, per-event stdin contract, 0/2 exit convention, persona front-matter convention, and this repo's bus.py/hiring sqlite -- proprietary 2025/2026 surfaces no general host-assertion or PR tool targets. Each file is small, stdlib-only (fits Windows/offline house constraints where goss/InSpec are weaker), and all 7 have live callers in claims-verify.jsonl with real runs logged today.

alternatives.covers: generic file-exists/service-running assertions -- maybe the trivial Path.exists() lines in hooks_exist.py.
alternatives.gap: zero vocabulary for Claude Code's hook JSON schema, per-event stdin contract, or this repo's bus.py/sqlite; nearly all 901 lines would still be hand-written.
alternatives.cost: not installed here (pip show confirms absent); Windows support historically limited per its own GitHub issue #601.
alternatives.maturity: actively documented; Windows support alpha/limited per issue tracker, confirmed via WebSearch.

alternatives.name: goss (YAML server-validation DSL)
alternatives.covers: same generic host-state assertions as testinfra, in YAML.
alternatives.gap: no concept of Claude Code hooks/personas/sqlite funnel; Windows support explicitly 'alpha' with feature-parity gaps.
alternatives.cost: not installed here (where goss empty); a Go binary+DSL for near-zero coverage gain.
alternatives.maturity: actively maintained; Windows alpha confirmed via WebSearch of goss docs/GitHub today.

alternatives.name: OPA/conftest (Rego policy over JSON/YAML/Terraform, ~0.68.2 as of Apr 2026)
alternatives.covers: the pure JSON-shape half of hooks_exist.py/bus_wired.py (hook on event X naming an existing script) as declarative policy instead of dict-walking+regex.
alternatives.gap: no subprocess/sqlite/hash I/O, so it can't do live hook invocation, hash diffing, sqlite counts, or sibling meta-testing -- most of the 901 lines.
alternatives.cost: not installed here (where conftest empty); new Go binary+DSL for coverage of roughly one file's shape logic.
alternatives.maturity: actively maintained, current release reconfirmed via WebSearch today.

alternatives.name: InSpec / Danger / reviewdog
alternatives.covers: InSpec: Ruby compliance DSL, same generic-surface gap plus a new language. Danger: PR-diff-time comment bot. reviewdog: formats linter output as PR annotations.
alternatives.gap: InSpec has no Claude Code resource pack. Danger/reviewdog act on PR diffs, not live local machine state; neither has an assertion language to express any of this logic.
alternatives.maturity: Danger/reviewdog not re-verified this session; named from prior knowledge, flagged as such.

migration_loc: 0 for check bodies (keep-ours). If split pursued for hooks_exist.py+bus_wired.py's shape-matching halves only: ~60-90 lines deleted, ~40-60 new Rego lines added -- a wash.
what_ours_does: 7 stdlib scripts, each a claim's verify body: agents_loadable.py parses persona front matter; bus_wired.py checks hook wiring; config_drift.py hash-diffs config files; hooks_exist.py resolves hook paths (Windows/Git-Bash); hooks_run.py launches hooks, flags broken exec; ledger_rows.py checks a sqlite funnel has rows; verifiers_fail_closed.py re-runs siblings w/ HOME emptied, asserts fail-closed.
strongest_counterargument: The JSON-shape-matching in hooks_exist.py/bus_wired.py (walking hooks groups, regex-sniffing paths in two dialects) is a generic 'does this JSON satisfy this policy' problem, exactly what Rego/conftest was built for. A split verdict is defensible for just those two files; one blanket keep-ours across all 7 understates that these two are the weakest members of the case.
